question: What claim about the nature of languages is being made with respect to what is heard and what is unheard?
premises: Languages take on forms of varied kinds.
Some of those linguistic forms are heard and others are unheard.
The distinction between heard and unheard holds among varied languages.
inference: Languages of varied forms include both heard and unheard kinds.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the distinction is ontological or experiential.
plain_english: Languages of varied forms are indeed heard and unheard.
